samples.title: Chronicle Backend
samples.tagline: Append an immutable fact and read one event source's history through a focused HTTP API.
highlights: Configure one named Chronicle event store
Use ConceptAs and EventSourceId for clear domain values and identities
Read the stored history without introducing a projection
limitations: The sample teaches the event log directly and intentionally leaves out projections and a frontend.
Its tests specify the Chronicle-facing behavior without starting external infrastructure.

samples.title: Chronicle Processing
samples.tagline: See one event stream feed a projection, reducer, and reactor without timing guesses.
highlights: Use ConceptAs values and an EventSourceId identity throughout the model
Compare a model-bound projection with a prior-state reducer
Return a deterministic follow-up event from a reactor
limitations: The endpoint uses fixed sample data so the processing styles stay in focus.
The sample is backend-only and uses local Chronicle development infrastructure.

samples.title: Idea Loom — Arc + React
samples.tagline: Build a polished command-and-query experience with generated contracts and no event sourcing.
highlights: Use ConceptAs values and validators in a model-bound Arc command
Generate TypeScript command, query, and read-model contracts
Compose React MVVM, an observable query, and a Cratis CommandDialog
limitations: The current-state store is in memory so the Arc and React boundary stays easy to see.
This sample deliberately does not use Chronicle.

samples.title: Chronicle Multi-Tenancy
samples.tagline: Use Arc header tenancy to isolate the same workflow in separate Chronicle namespaces.
highlights: Resolve the tenant from Arc's standard header
Map tenant context to Chronicle namespaces
Use the same EventSourceId safely in tenant A, tenant B, and Default
limitations: The tenant header selects context but is not an authorization policy.
The sample is backend-only and uses local development infrastructure.

samples.title: Chronicle Cross-Store
samples.tagline: Connect two named event stores through a typed outbox, filtered inbox, and local translation.
highlights: Keep Orders and Fulfillment in separate event stores
Forward one narrow contract through source outbox and target inbox
Translate the contract into a target-owned event and read model
limitations: Cross-store processing is asynchronous and is not a distributed transaction.
The sample does not claim exactly-once delivery.

samples.title: Chronicle with ASP.NET Core
samples.tagline: Host the same event-processing concepts behind a small HTTP API.
highlights: Configure Chronicle through ASP.NET Core dependency injection
Register reducers, projections, reactors, and query services
Append events through minimal HTTP endpoints
limitations: The sample concentrates on backend hosting and does not include a browser frontend.
Its HTTP surface is deliberately small.

samples.title: Chronicle Operations Diagnosis
samples.tagline: Create one deterministic failed partition and find it with the CLI and Workbench.
highlights: Use typed probe identity and name values
Create one stable reactor failure
Inspect the event, observer, and failed partition without repair actions
limitations: The POST endpoint intentionally creates local fixture data.
Replay, retry, quarantine changes, redaction, and administration are outside the sample.

samples.title: Model-First Library
samples.tagline: Compile one Screenplay model and run its accepted and rejected examples through Stage.
highlights: Describe concepts, a command, validation, and an event in one model
Keep accepted and rejected examples beside the behavior
Compile with Screenplay and run model specifications with Stage
limitations: The sample verifies the model and its specifications without running a live Chronicle command.
Scene UI, source generation, and Studio round trips are intentionally outside this first step.

samples.title: Library
samples.tagline: Tour a larger Cratis application with separate lending and membership experiences.
highlights: Organize behavior as cohesive vertical slices
Generate TypeScript contracts from backend commands and queries
Compose separate lending and membership applications for local development
limitations: The MongoDB profile is the current reference path for the demonstrated read models.
Some domain flows are backend examples and are not yet represented by a dedicated screen.
